Ты — исполнитель live-spec. Готовишь к доставке ПОСЛЕДНИЙ пакет дня — вынос навыка text-audit в свой дом. Пакет сделан утром и стоит на старом main; сведи его с сегодняшним. НЕ ПУШИТЬ, доставку делает координатор.

## Пакет
Ветка `lane/2026-08-18-textaudit-out`, коммит `34f02abe`, копия `/private/tmp/live-spec-textaudit/wt`. Доклад: `/private/tmp/live-spec-control/textaudit-out-report-2026-08-18.md` — прочитай первым.
Суть: 13 сварных швов расшито, тело навыка ужато 30 895 → 16 048 Б, в доме остаётся тонкий адаптер `skills/text-audit-pack/SKILL.md` по образцу пакета прувера плюс `.text-audit/lints.json`, порог живых навыков опущен 9 → 8, разрезана связь, по которой `scripts/gen-language-consumers.py` ПОРОЖДАЛ часть навыка. Содержимое будущего отдельного репозитория лежит в `/private/tmp/live-spec-textaudit/out` — оно НЕ едет в main, дом наружу заводит владелец.

## Что изменилось в main за день (с чем сводить)
Восемь пакетов: судьи (opt-in, требование 311), матрица (13 строк), храповик, README+прувер, починка тестовой изоляции (`tests/conftest.py` снимает девять переменных git, ловец `judged_tree_gains_no_commits`), вырезанный счётчик строк навыков (README + `guardrails/tree-counts.json`), разметка очереди, и САМОЕ КРУПНОЕ — РАСПИЛ СПЕКИ: `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` теперь ядро ~50 КБ плюс тридцать файлов `spec/*.md`, а проверки читают спеку через общий узел, а не по пути. Твой пакет наверняка трогает спеку и реестр проверок — учитывай новую раскладку.

## Работа
1. `cd ~/live-spec && git fetch -q`, свежая копия от текущего origin/main: `git worktree add -b deliver/textaudit /private/tmp/live-spec-dt/wt <хэш origin/main>`.
2. ПЕРЕД слиянием посмотри авторов вершины: `git log --format='%h %an <%ae> %s' -3 lane/2026-08-18-textaudit-out`. Если увидишь `t <t@t>`, `gate@example.com`, `fixture@example.invalid` — НЕ сливай, зови меня: одна ветка сегодня так обросла тремя сотнями фикстурных коммитов, удаляющих полрепозитория.
3. Влей ветку слиянием (не rebase). Конфликты разрешай ПОСТРОЧНО по смыслу, никогда не бери сторону целиком. Требования, уехавшие в `spec/*.md`, ищи там, а не в ядре.
4. Точечные тесты по тронутому: язык, реестр проверок, трассировка, тесты навыков. Полный набор НЕ гоняй.
5. Пересобери генерируемое штатными скриптами, если разошлось.
6. Проверь авторство своих коммитов, при следах фикстур — `git commit --amend --reset-author --no-edit` (только незапушенное).

## Границы
- НЕ ПУШИТЬ. Не создавать ничего на GitHub. Запрещены reset/rebase/stash/clean и `git checkout -- <файл>`.
- Не трогай ~/.claude, ~/live-spec, чужие копии (-ds, -dj, -dm, -dr, -drm, -gitenv, -cull, -backlog, -exam2).
- Коммиты явными путями.

Ответь не более чем 10 строками: копия и ветка, какие конфликты и как разрешены, что с байтами навыка, какие тесты прогнал, что не закрыто.

Копия: `/private/tmp/live-spec-textaudit/wt` (worktree `lane/2026-08-18-textaudit-out` от `23d2495`).
Коммит: `34f02ab`. Содержимое для будущего репозитория: `/private/tmp/live-spec-textaudit/out`.

## 1. Сварные швы — что нашлось и чем закрыто

Список ревьюера (`skill-classification.md`) назвал контракт из трёх пунктов и пять доков-доказательств.
Проверка на месте нашла один шов, которого в списке ревьюера не было — он оказался самым глубоким.

| # | Шов | Где сидел | Чем закрыт |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Генерация двух reference-файлов из пакетного источника.** `scripts/gen-language-consumers.py` строил `skills/text-audit/references/reader-prompt.md` целиком и сплайсил блок в `references/human-prose-rules.md` из `guardrails/language-rules.json` на каждом прогоне; `guardrails/check-language-rules.py` держал оба файла тестом на дрейф от свежей сборки. Это НЕ в списке ревьюера. Если бы навык просто убрать, `check-language-rules.py` сразу краснел бы («reader-prompt.md is absent — it is generated output»), гейт b падал. | `scripts/gen-language-consumers.py`, `guardrails/check-language-rules.py` | Обе функции-генераторы (`build_reader_prompt`, `render_human_prose_rules`, `shipped_case`, `human_prose_definition`, `reader_prompt_rules`, `render_reader_prompt_stops`) и их записи в `outputs`/`SPLICED`/`build_blocks`/`validate` удалены; гейт больше не ждёт эти два файла. В `out/references/*.md` содержимое заморожено как статичный снимок на 2026-08-18 с переписанной шапкой (без ссылки на генератор). |
| 2 | `scripts/check-registry.json` держал `reach` для `check-language-rules.py`, указывающий на оба удалённых пути | `scripts/check-registry.json` | `reach` заменён на `docs/language-rules.md` / `docs/language-rule-coverage.md` — то, что гейт реально теперь читает |

| 8 | **«The pack this skill belongs to»** — ростер всех 11 скиллов пакета | тело SKILL.md, конец файла | Вырезан целиком |
| 9 | **Round/«cheap reader» определение** — правило 74ef247 ввело пару «сильный+дешёвый» читатель, но нигде не было явно сказано, что «дешёвый» означает именно «без загруженных скиллов/правил дома» | тело SKILL.md, «The loop» | В `out/SKILL.md` — общая формулировка («no project skills or rules»); в доме — точная формулировка слова владельца в `skills/text-audit-pack/SKILL.md`, раздел «What a cheap reader means run inside this pack» |
| 10 | **Список-ростер пакета** («The pack, whole:» / «The pack this skill belongs to») в 5 чужих скиллах (`communicator`, `design-reviewer`, `feedback-intake`, `live-spec-base`, `test-author`) + `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, `README.md`, `OVERVIEW.md` — паритет-тест `TestPackListParity` требует, чтобы имя каждой директории `skills/*` встречалось во всех этих списках | 8 файлов | Везде добавлено `text-audit-pack` рядом с `text-audit`, по образцу `product-prover`/`product-prover-pack`. `OVERVIEW.md`: «Ten working skills» → «Eleven» (там продукт-провер-пак уже считался отдельным пунктом ростера, так что паритет сохранён). `live-spec-base`/`ARCHITECTURE.md`/`build-pipeline` «ten working skills» — НЕ трогал: там счёт исторически идёт по концептуальным «working skills» (10, включая внешний text-audit, но не считая адаптеры), несогласованность с OVERVIEW.md старая и не моя |

Прогнано и с `TEXT_AUDIT_LINT_ROOT`, и без — оба режима зелёные |

| 13 | `evals/fixtures/text-audit/*.md` (3 фикстуры) — использовались только уехавшим тестом | `evals/fixtures/` | Удалены из дома, копия в `out/fixtures/`. `evals/text-audit.md` (пакетный eval-сценарий с другим текстом) НЕ трогал — не пересекается |

## 2. Было → стало, байты

- `skills/text-audit/SKILL.md`: **30895 → 16048** байт в `out/SKILL.md` (−48%). Цель была «примерно 11К» — не дотянул, честно: дальнейшая резка начинала терять операционное содержание (сама петля, механические линты, cold-reader контракт), а не «сварку». Основной вес после чистки — законная субстанция навыка, не мусор дома.
- `README.md`: 5683 → 5357 байт (install-инструкция стала «это канонiчный репо», не зеркало; убран футер про «read-only mirror»).
- `references/*.md` — не резались (это не входило в цель «31К→11К», у неё была ~31К именно у SKILL.md); только вырезана шапка про генератор в двух файлах:
  - `reader-prompt.md`: 8241 → 8353 (шапка чуть длиннее — честно объясняет, что копия статична);
  - `human-prose-rules.md`: 24226 → 24068.
- `LICENSE`, `rewrite-meaning-check.md`, `unprompted-reader-brief.md` — без изменений (79238 байт всего тела навыка в доме → 79860 байт в `out/` целиком, включая новые тесты/fixtures/README, которых раньше не было отдельным счётом).
- Дом: `git diff --stat 23d2495..HEAD` → 28 файлов, +175/−1699 строк.

## 3. Что лежит в `out/` — готово к переезду

```
out/
  SKILL.md              (16048 байт, version 1.0.0, без пакетной сварки)
  README.md             (канонiчный, install из своего репо)
  LICENSE
  references/
    reader-prompt.md            (заморожен, статичная копия на 2026-08-18)
    human-prose-rules.md        (заморожен, статичная копия на 2026-08-18)
    rewrite-meaning-check.md    (без изменений)
    unprompted-reader-brief.md  (без изменений)
  tests/
    test_reader_prompt_shape.py   (адаптирован, без пакетного docs/language-defects.md)
    test_text_audit_fixtures.py   (адаптирован, линты — опционально через TEXT_AUDIT_LINT_ROOT)
  fixtures/
    ambiguous-explanation.md
    clean-prose-wrong-command.md
    rewrite-weakens-the-rule.md
```
Ничего не выдумано сверх существовавшего — только перенос, заморозка и вырезание пакетной сварки.
Заготовки прогнаны у себя (`python3 -m pytest tests/` внутри `out/` — 11 passed, 4 skipped без
`TEXT_AUDIT_LINT_ROOT`; 15 passed при `TEXT_AUDIT_LINT_ROOT=<путь до дома>`).

## 4. Адаптер в доме

`skills/text-audit-pack/SKILL.md` (по образцу `product-prover-pack`, `requires: text-audit >= 1.0.0`):
таблица шести линтов пакета, пояснение почему `check-language-rules.py` в их число не входит,
пути пакета, раздел «Where the rule home moved» (честно про обрыв генерации) и раздел
**«What a cheap reader means run inside this pack»** — там стоит требуемая строка: дешёвый читатель =
без загруженных скиллов/правил дома, со ссылкой на правило 74ef247 и слово владельца 18.08. Тот же
коммит `34f02ab`.

`.text-audit/lints.json` — новый файл, host-контракт line, шесть команд по образцу описанного в
классификации.

`.gitignore` — добавлена строка `skills/text-audit/` (по образцу `product-prover/`), с честной
оговоркой, что `install-external-skills.sh` пока НЕ умеет её ставить (однoскилловый).

## 5. Тесты и гейты, что гонял

- `pytest tests/test_traceability.py tests/test_language_rules.py tests/test_check_registry.py` — 224
  passed (до и после коммита).
- `pytest tests/test_traceability.py -k TestPackListParity` — точечно, до и после каждой правки
  ростера.
- `guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py` — красный дважды по пути (адаптер без записи в цензе;
  затем длинное предложение в README подняло census 4→5), оба раза почистил и перегнал
  `scripts/rule-census.py --json guardrails/rule-census.json`; финально зелёный (141 doc, cap 25).
- `guardrails/check-language-rules.py`, `guardrails/check-named-checks.py`,
  `guardrails/check-index-generated.py PRODUCT_SPEC.md PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md`,
  `bash guardrails/check-freeze.sh` — все зелёные.
- `scripts/spec-style-lint.py skills/text-audit-pack/SKILL.md` — гонял до и после фикса (2 ошибки →
  0); census `long` для адаптера 11 → 6 (для сравнения у `product-prover-pack` — 7, так что в норме).
- После каждого прогона — `git log --oneline 23d2495..HEAD` и `git status --porcelain`: фиктивных
  коммитов и пропавших файлов не встретил ни разу.
- Полный набор (весь `tests/`) не гонял — по инструкции.

## 6. Что осталось незакрытым (честно)

14	## First pass (2026-08-18, against 99050f5..HEAD before d432fca9) — REJECT
15	
16	First-pass verdict: REJECT. One of the four trims silently drops the rule's mechanism instead of
17	pointing at it, and both new pointers name a filename two files in this project share without saying
18	which one.
19	
20	## What changed
21	
22	`skills/communicator/SKILL.md`'s calque bullet and no-contrast-frame bullet, and
23	`writing-register.md`'s rule 15 (twice), traded a restated law for a pointer to its home. Read against
24	`git show 99050f5` and the current text of both files in full.
25	
26	## Findings
27	
28	1. **SKILL.md's rule-15 fallback bullet lost the mechanism it exists to carry, not just its
29	   paraphrase.** `SKILL.md` line 431 now reads: *"Never the contrast frame (rule 15, ... — Home:
30	   profile.md key language.no-contrast-frame). The linter's scissors check holds the floor..."* — the
31	   whole definition of what a contrast frame IS (the em-dash/comma shape, the Russian equivalents,
32	   "say what the thing is") is gone, replaced by nothing but the Home pointer. This is the section
33	   whose own framing sentence (line 427) says it "holds only the two loudest rules so a reader meets
34	   them even without loading [writing-register.md]". A reader who takes that promise at face value
35	   and does not load writing-register.md now has zero mechanism to apply — only a pointer to a
36	   *different* file than the one this section exists to stand in for, and (finding 2) an ambiguous one.
37	   Contrast this with `writing-register.md`'s own rule 15 (lines 93-104): it trimmed only the
38	   redundant intro sentence and **kept** the shapes bullet ("the em-dash or a comma leading into the
39	   denied neighbour..."), so that file's own checklist item 9 ("scan ... for rule 15's shapes") still
40	   resolves inside the same document. SKILL.md's copy has no such fallback — it is a genuine
41	   information loss, not a dedup.
42	
43	2. **The pointer's own text is ambiguous between two files literally named `profile.md` in this
44	   project.** Both new pointers read "Home: profile.md key language.no-contrast-frame" with no
45	   qualifier. This repo carries a *host* profile at `.live-spec/profile.md` (checked directly: it has
46	   no `language.*` keys at all — its bullets are `prover.cadence`, `project.kind`, `trust.push-grant`,
47	   etc.) and a *personal* profile at `~/.claude/live-spec/profile.md` (a symlink to
48	   `~/.claude/playbook/personal/profile.md`, a machine-wide file outside this repository, checked
49	   directly: its `## Language` section does carry `no-calques` and `no-contrast-frame` bullets with
50	   the full rule text). The pack's own vocabulary (OVERVIEW.md's table, TEST_MATRIX M-233 — "the law's
51	   home named (**personal** profile language.no-scissors)") always disambiguates with the word
52	   "personal" precisely because two same-named files exist. Both new pointers drop that word. A model
53	   resolving "profile.md" against the current tree, as bare filenames normally resolve, lands on
54	   `.live-spec/profile.md` and finds nothing — the law's actual text lives one directory scope further
55	   out, on a file that (per TEST_MATRIX M-208) is not guaranteed to exist on every host at all.
56	
57	3. **No dangling reference otherwise, and the surviving pointer is sound.** SKILL.md's calque bullet
58	   ("base rule 2, no-calques") points into `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md` rule 2 (read directly,
59	   lines 87-96), which fully states the mechanism — docs-language terms never loan-translate into
60	   chat, say it in plain chat words, the original may trail in parentheses. That pointer resolves
61	   inside the shipped pack, with no ambiguity and no loss; it is the one trim of the four that works
62	   as designed.
63	
64	4. **No orphaned fragments.** Read every edited line in full context (not just the diff hunks): no
65	   sentence is left starting mid-clause or missing a verb after the cuts. The em-dash lead-in before
66	   the calque bullet's worked example ("... no-calques). — *❌ ..."*) predates this commit and is
67	   unchanged.
68	
69	## The net
70	
71	Three of four trims are clean or acceptable; one drops instruction outright (finding 1) and both new
72	"Home:" pointers are ambiguous in a way this project's own conventions normally guard against
73	(finding 2). Not a formality rejection — a reader following either pointer as literally written, on a
74	fresh host or without already knowing the personal-profile convention, cannot recover the law.
75

77	and `skills/communicator/references/writing-register.md`, `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md` rule 2,
78	`.live-spec/profile.md` in full, and `~/.claude/playbook/personal/profile.md`'s `## Language` section

86	  (rule 15, ... — Home: personal profile `language.no-contrast-frame`). Never name a thing by denying
87	  its neighbour (an em-dash or comma leading into the denied alternative, and the parallel Russian

2	name: text-audit-pack
3	description: 'Pack-side bindings for the external text-audit skill inside the live-spec pack. It carries what the audit body no longer does: the pack''s own mechanical lints (declared in .text-audit/lints.json), the reading-record home, and what a cheap reader means run inside this pack. Load it whenever text-audit runs inside a live-spec project. It audits nothing itself.'
4	metadata:
5	  version: 5.0.0
6	  requires: text-audit >= 1.0.0 (github.com/happysasha18/text-audit)
7	---
8	
9	# text-audit — pack bindings
10	
11	text-audit is an external skill with its own repository and version line. This page binds it to the
12	live-spec pack. An audit run inside a live-spec project reads the audit skill's own SKILL.md first and
13	this page beside it. An audit run anywhere else needs nothing from this page.
14	
15	## The mechanical lints this pack declares
16	
17	`text-audit`'s Step 1 runs every command a host names in `.text-audit/lints.json` before it falls back
18	to its own bundled grep. This pack's copy, at the repository root, names the six scripts that carried
19	these classes when the audit body still lived here:
20	
21	| Script | Class it catches | Surface |
22	| ------ | ----------------- | ------- |
23	| `guardrails/check-vocabulary.py` | a term used with no definition at first use | spec body |
24	| `guardrails/check-weak-words.py` | a weak relational word with an unfilled slot | spec body |
25	| `guardrails/check-requirement-shape.py` | a spec section missing the requirements genre | spec body |
26	| `scripts/spec-style-lint.py` | style and register, spec-body word cap | spec body |
27	| `scripts/preshow-register-lint.py` | style and register, any human-facing surface | any |
28	| `guardrails/check-one-name.py` | one thing answering to two names | any |
29	
30	`guardrails/check-language-rules.py` is this pack's own gate over `guardrails/language-rules.json` and
31	the pages generated from it, a separate document from the six above. It takes no audited-file argument
32	and reports nothing about a text under audit. Before the 2026-08-18 extraction it also held two of
33	text-audit's own reference pages to a generated-drift test. That arm is retired (see "Where the rule
34	home moved," below), and this gate now checks only this pack's own documents.
35	
36	## Pack paths
37	
38	- the reading record home — `docs/language-reads/`, one dated file per reading, matching the record
39	  shape `docs/language-defects.md` and `docs/language-rule-coverage.md` already describe;
40	- the comprehension gate that calls this loop — `spec-author`'s "The comprehension gate" section,
41	  which names text-audit by skill reference and names no path;
42	- `docs/language-defects.md` — this pack's own record of why each language rule says what it says,
43	  written before text-audit existed as a general-purpose skill; it still cites text-audit's reading
44	  loop as evidence, and a reader following that citation now leaves the pack.
45	
46	## Where the rule home moved
47	
48	Before the extraction, `guardrails/language-rules.json` was the one editable home for the human-prose
49	rules. `scripts/gen-language-consumers.py` built text-audit's `references/reader-prompt.md` and
50	`references/human-prose-rules.md` off it on every run. Both files now ship as a static, hand-kept
51	snapshot inside the external skill's own repository, frozen as of 2026-08-18. A rule added to
52	`guardrails/language-rules.json` after that date still reaches this pack's own writer's and
53	maintainer's pages (`docs/language-rules.md`, `docs/language-rule-coverage.md`) and the model judge's
54	law bodies (`hooks/language-laws.json`). It no longer reaches the audit skill's bundled rule sheet. A
55	project that wants the fuller, moving rule set points its own `.text-audit/lints.json` at a script
56	reading this pack's rule home directly. None does yet, so the bundled snapshot is what a text-audit
57	run inside this pack holds a text to today.
58	
59	## What a cheap reader means run inside this pack
60	
61	A **reading round**, as text-audit's own body defines it, is one pass by each of its two readers, and
62	both readers of a round are cheap readers. Run inside this pack, that definition takes one more line.
63	The owner's word on 2026-08-18 settles it, following rule 74ef247, which first split a round into one
64	strong and one cheap reader: **a cheap reader is a reader with none of this pack's own skills or rules
65	loaded** — no `live-spec-base`, no working skill, no base rule, nothing this pack would hand a worker
66	starting ordinary pipeline work. A fresh session still carrying this pack's skills or rules is not
67	cheap by this pack's own accounting, whatever budget tier ran it. A reading run under one does not
68	count toward the two clean rounds this pack's comprehension gate closes on.
69	
70	## Version discipline
71	
72	`scripts/install-external-skills.sh` is single-skill today and does not yet install text-audit. A
73	checkout under `skills/text-audit/` (gitignored, matching `skills/product-prover/`) is manual until
74	that installer grows a second target. Once it does, the same discipline as product-prover-pack applies:
75	the installer refuses a version below the minimum in this page's metadata, and the installed copy is
76	never tracked by this repository. The external repository is its only source of truth, and raising the
77	minimum here is a pack change that lands as one.
78

2	name: product-prover-pack
3	description: 'Pack-side bindings for the external product-prover skill inside the live-spec pack. It carries what the prover body no longer does: the pin map from this pack''s PRODUCT_SPEC requirement codes to prover lenses, the pack paths a review reads, the record home and shape the push gate checks, and the mode names the build pipeline uses. Load it whenever product-prover runs inside a live-spec project. It reviews nothing itself.'
4	metadata:
5	  version: 5.0.0
6	  requires: product-prover >= 1.3.0 (github.com/happysasha18/product-prover)
7	---
8	
9	# Product Prover — pack bindings
10	
11	The prover is an external skill with its own repository and version line. This page binds it to the
12	live-spec pack. A review run inside a live-spec project reads the prover's own SKILL.md first and
13	this page beside it. A review run anywhere else needs nothing from this page.
14	
15	## Mode names
16	
17	The build pipeline asks for a mode by machine name, and the prover answers to both name sets:
18	
19	| Pipeline name | Prover name         |
20	| ------------- | ------------------- |
21	| `FULL`        | Full review         |
22	| `CROSS-LINK`  | New-surface review  |
23	| `FEATURE-FIT` | Feature-fit review  |
24	
25	## Pack paths
26	
27	Where the prover speaks of the reviewed project's documents, this pack keeps them at:
28	
29	- surface registry — `SURFACES.md`
30	- the spec under review — `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, its code index in `PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md`
31	- the architecture under review — `ARCHITECTURE.md`
32	- the build walk's stations — `docs/pipeline.md`
33	- lens histories — `docs/lenses.md`
34	- the queue — `ROADMAP.md`
35	
36	`base rule n` names a numbered rule in `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md`. `P9` is the architecture
37	principle that every cross-cutting law owes a test row on each surface it governs, carried in
38	`skills/test-author/SKILL.md`.
39	
40	## The record
41	
42	A review inside this pack writes its record to `docs/prover/` as `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` and commits
43	it. `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh` is the gate that reads it; `docs/prover/README.md` holds the
44	shape. A record covering a push carries the `PUSH-REVIEW` marker and the fields `Range:`,
45	`Files read:`, `Checks run:`, `Findings:`, and `Blocking:`, each with a value. The record's opening
46	line names the prover version that ran, and the gate's freshness arms hold the record against the
47	last change to each guarded document.
48	
49	A minor (`x.Y.0`) bump of this pack requires a `FULL` pass
50	(`skills/build-pipeline/references/minor-bump-gate.md`).
51	
52	## Pin map
53	
54	Each pack requirement below is carried by the named prover lens. The requirement's text lives in
55	`PRODUCT_SPEC.md`; the lens's mechanics live in the prover. When a lens moves or renames in a prover
56	release, this table is the one place the pack updates.
57	
58	| Requirement | Prover home |
59	| ----------- | ----------- |
60	| INV-114 | How to write findings; Reviewing a rewrite before it merges |
61	| INV-141 | Work that belongs elsewhere; Cross-surface policy uniformity |
62	| INV-30, INV-31, INV-72, INV-138 | Edge-condition completeness |
63	| INV-125 | Cross-surface policy uniformity |
64	| INV-126, INV-127, INV-165, INV-167 | Lifecycle |
65	| INV-72 | Unwritten seams; Interactive overlap across layers; Edge-condition completeness |
66	| INV-136 | Interactive overlap across layers |
67	| INV-128, INV-144 | Three-source disagreement |
68	| INV-49 | False-serialization and over-broad independence edge |
69	| INV-244, INV-248 | Delivery separability along a declared axis |
70	| INV-101 | Declared cross-cutting laws |
71	| INV-169 | The second-sibling question (feature-fit review) |
72	| INV-170 | The quantifier re-verify (new-surface review) |
73	| INV-215 | The cognitive-load lens, its reading-load reading |
74	| INV-233 | The node-growth re-ask (architecture lens) |
75	
76	## Version discipline
77	
78	`scripts/install-external-skills.sh` installs the prover and refuses a version below the minimum in
79	this page's metadata. The installed copy under `skills/product-prover/` is not tracked by this
80	repository; the external repository is its only source of truth. Raising the minimum here is a pack
81	change and lands as one.
82	
83	## The pack's lens bindings
84	
85	This page is written against `live-spec-base` (v5.0.0). The bindings below are the pack-side review
86	duties a live-spec project adds to the external prover's own lenses. The prover's body states the
87	general method; each line here is the pack's concrete pin of one duty, read beside the body on every
88	review run inside a live-spec project.
89	
90	- **Unwritten seams [INV-72].** For every surface the document places before a user, the review walks
91	  every other surface that can be present at the same time and asks what happens at the seam; a
92	  reachable situation with a blank answer is a finding. The reviewer reports the blank and invents no
93	  answer. The headline of this duty is the unwritten seam.
94	- **Entry symmetry (SPEC INV-50).** A conditionally-entered face with no deliberate re-entry path is a
95	  finding, and a written one-way counts as an answer.
96	- **Domain language on every user-facing surface.** The review holds every user-facing string to one
97	  bar: read them as the user would; a leaked internal word is a finding.
98	- **The architecture lens, seven items.** Beside spec-fact ownership and named seams, the review checks
99	  that the quality budgets are stated with their instrumentation homes and watchers — each names its
100	  watcher — that the runtime view walks every promised flow, that the placement view says where
101	  every node runs, and that each grown node re-answers its fitness questions (the node-growth
102	  re-ask).
103	- **Unbacked surfaces and unlabelled sketches.** A surface no requirement backs, or a sketch shown
104	  without its label, is a finding; the stress families of questions in the prover's own reference run
105	  over each.
106	- **Gaps, never taste.** The review's output bar is: Report gaps. Taste is out of scope. What reads
107	  as a preference goes to the design reviewer or the human, never into a finding.
108	- **The norm lens.** An approved prototype cited as `norm: <path>` is the definition the build answers
109	  to; a plan contradicting its own artifact is a finding.
110	- **The record names its reviewer.** Every record closes naming the prover skill version it ran under,
111	  so a spec proven under an old lens set never keeps a silent green.
112	- **The class lens (SPEC INV-124).** The prover's class lens is the document-side face of the
113	  confirmed-bug class hunt: the three questions it asks on a filed defect are how the hunt reaches
114	  the document, and its class line lands in the record beside the other verdicts.
115	- **Member of the review-record class (SPEC INV-156).** The record a review writes under
116	  `docs/prover/` is one member of the review-record class the pack's spec declares once — the shared
117	  dated-file shape every review pass in this pack writes.
118	- **Clean-context release review (SPEC INV-237).** A release of this pack runs its adversarial pass
119	  from a fresh, differently-contexted seat that authored none of the release's changes, and a newly
120	  grown lens or rule is self-applied to its own introducing document before release.
121

44:    echo "FAIL (loadability): $dir_name — no 'Work that belongs elsewhere' section (row 80)"; fail=1
---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-skill-loadability.sh — gate (f) of the push gate: every shipped skill LOADS
# (row 80, the Trail-of-Bits lesson). A skill that ships with broken frontmatter, a
# name that doesn't match its folder, no description, no version, or a "when NOT to
# use" section missing, is RED at push — a skill the harness can't index or a reader
# can't scope is a broken artifact however good its prose.
#
# Usage: check-skill-loadability.sh [skills-dir]
#   skills-dir defaults to "<repo-root>/skills"

set -euo pipefail

SKILLS_DIR="${1:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/skills}"

fail=0
count=0
for skill_md in "$SKILLS_DIR"/*/SKILL.md; do
  [ -f "$skill_md" ] || continue
  count=$((count+1))
  dir_name="$(basename "$(dirname "$skill_md")")"

  # frontmatter block: first line ---, a closing --- within the first 40 lines
  if [ "$(head -1 "$skill_md")" != "---" ] || ! sed -n '2,40p' "$skill_md" | grep -q '^---$'; then
    echo "FAIL (loadability): $dir_name — no frontmatter block"; fail=1; continue
  fi
  fm="$(awk '/^---$/{n++; next} n==1{print} n>=2{exit}' "$skill_md")"

  name="$(sed -n 's/^name:[[:space:]]*//p' <<<"$fm" | head -1)"
  if [ -z "$name" ]; then
    echo "FAIL (loadability): $dir_name — frontmatter has no name:"; fail=1
  elif [ "$name" != "$dir_name" ]; then
    echo "FAIL (loadability): $dir_name — name '$name' does not match its folder"; fail=1
  fi

  if ! printf '%s\n' "$fm" | grep -q '^description:'; then
    echo "FAIL (loadability): $dir_name — frontmatter has no description:"; fail=1
  fi

  if ! printf '%s\n' "$fm" | grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]+version:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'; then
    echo "FAIL (loadability): $dir_name — no metadata version (M-7)"; fail=1
  fi

  if ! grep -qi 'work that belongs elsewhere' "$skill_md"; then
    echo "FAIL (loadability): $dir_name — no 'Work that belongs elsewhere' section (row 80)"; fail=1
  fi
done

if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL (loadability): no skills found under $SKILLS_DIR"; exit 1
fi

if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "  Fix: repair the skill's frontmatter/section; a skill that can't load or scope itself must not ship."
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK (loadability): $count skill(s) load, named, versioned, negative-scoped."
exit 0

# R5 — pricing the 53 rules outside the shared rulebook

Pins verified by `guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh` (its r5 leg, ROADMAP row 588) — run it after any edit to a home file above; a rotted `path:start-end` pin reds.

Root: the frozen plan `.live-spec/culling-plan-v3-2026-08-10.md`, step R5. The day 1 census, `.live-spec/day1-census-rules.md`, measured only the 35 rules in `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md`. The plan's queue for the next phase runs from the most expensive rule first, and it needs a price for every rule the day 1 census left out. This page prices those rules: the ones that live inside the nine working skill files rather than the shared rulebook.

## The count check

`NEXT_STEPS.md:15` today does not carry the 88-rule claim. The line that names it moved to `NEXT_STEPS.md:26` ("Rules cut: 0 of 88."), because the live-state block above it grew between when the plan cited line 15 and today. The citation drifted with that edit. The number itself holds steady: 88 total rules, 35 shared plus 53 in the working skills, is stated in three places — `.live-spec/culling-plan-v2-2026-08-09.md` line 18, `.live-spec/handover-2026-08-09.md` line 40, and `NEXT_STEPS.md` line 26.

**Finding the 53.** Neither the plan nor the day 1 census writes down how a "rule" is told apart from a process step inside a working skill's file. The day 1 census identified all 35 rules in `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md` the same way: each is a top-level numbered list item with a bold lead-in sentence, for example line 110, `1. **Ask, never guess.** A gap only the human can fill...`. Applying that same shape — a line matching `^[0-9]+\. \*\*` at the start of the line, inside the skill's own `SKILL.md` body — to the nine working skills (`build-pipeline`, `communicator`, `design-reviewer`, `feedback-intake`, `product-prover`, `publish`, `spec-author`, `test-author`, `text-audit`) returns exactly 53 items. `feedback-collector` is not one of the nine: its own file states it is "off by default" and silent unless a host turns it on, so it sits outside the working set the plan counts (`skills/feedback-collector/SKILL.md` line 22).

This shape does not match every skill evenly. Three skills — `product-prover`, `publish`, and `feedback-intake` — carry numbered lists too, but none of their numbered items open with a bold lead-in phrase, so this method counts zero rules in each of them. `communicator` carries its own explicit list of twenty-two items it calls rules and marks `(rule 1)` through `(rule 22)`; those are written with dashes, so this method skips them. The six items this method counts inside `communicator` come from a different, numbered list further down the same file, "the pre-report walk." The count still lands on exactly 53, the same number the plan states. That match is this session's own reading of an undefined convention landing on the plan's number, worth flagging as a coincidence to confirm rather than treating as settled. A session that instead counted communicator's twenty-two self-declared rules, or counted every numbered list regardless of bold lead-in (which would add product-prover's and publish's process lists), would reach a different number. This gap in the method is itself worth a line in the plan.

**Method for each column below.**

- **Home file** — the skill's `SKILL.md`, with the line range the rule's own text occupies. A rule's span runs from its own numbered line to the line before the next numbered item in the same list, or the next heading, whichever comes first — the same boundary rule day 1 used to keep one rule's text from swallowing its neighbor's.
- **Opening line** — the rule's own first line, quoted exactly as written, numeral and bold lead-in included.
- **Body bytes** — `len(text.encode("utf-8"))` over the exact line range above, counted with a short Python script reading each file directly (the same unit day 1 used for the 35 shared rules).
- **Pinned tests** — a rule's own SPEC codes (`INV-`, `T-`, `E-`, `ACT-`, `M-`, `A-` followed by a number), read out of its body text, searched with `grep -rlF '<code>' tests/` and counted as the union of distinct files any of its codes hit. Nineteen of the 53 rules cite no such code in their own text; for those, the search falls back to the rule's bold lead-in phrase itself (quotation marks and markdown stripped) as the `grep -rlF` pattern, and the exact phrase used is named next to each such row. A rule with no code and a lead-in too generic to search safely ("Purpose", "Entities", "Actors") still ran the same search on that word and returned zero, which the table reports as zero rather than skipping the row.
- **Price** — body bytes plus pinned-test count, the plan's own starting cost measure (`.live-spec/culling-plan-v3-2026-08-10.md` line 86).

**Totals.** 53 rules found. 43,753 body bytes in all. 314 pinned-test hits in all, summed across rules (a test file pinning more than one rule is counted again for each). Combined price: 44,067.

**Repaired at HEAD.** The pins above were re-derived against commit `a5b94f85b8bd607e0ff462eb9e07e0c96235354d` (2026-08-12): every row's home file, line range, body bytes and pinned-test count were re-measured by the same methods stated above. No row's price-rank order changed.

Every affected row's home path and line range was re-derived by matching its exact text in the new tree. No rule's text, body-byte count, pinned-test count or price changed, and no row's price-rank order changed: the move was verbatim.

**Re-measured after the build-pipeline prose pass (2026-08-18).** `skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md` was rewritten sentence by sentence for readability, so all nine build-pipeline rows were re-derived by the methods stated above: the span rule, `len(text.encode("utf-8"))` over that span, and the union of `grep -rlF` hits for the rule's own codes. 6

8	
9	`NEXT_STEPS.md:15` today does not carry the 88-rule claim. The count still lands on exactly 53, the same number the plan states. That match is this session's own reading of an undefined convention landing on the plan's number, worth flagging as a coincidence to confirm rather than treating as settled. A session that instead counted communicator's twenty-two self-declared rules, or counted every numbered list regardless of bold lead-in (which would add product-prover's and publish's process lists), would reach a different number. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# check-skill-review.sh — gate (s) of the push gate: a push that substantively changes a skill
3	# reds unless a skill-creator review record for that change is committed (SPEC INV-208, ROADMAP 419).
4	#
5	# THE LAW (the owner's word, 2026-07-17 ~18:26): the session is leaned on to remember to run Anthropic's
6	# skill-creator review whenever a skill is modified, and the session forgets — a reminder does not
7	# hold. So the habit becomes a machine: when a diff about to be pushed changes a skill's body, the
8	# push reds until a matching review record exists. This is the same shape as check-prover-record.sh,
9	# which reds a push whose spec/architecture delta carries no fresh prover record.
10	#
11	# Usage: check-skill-review.sh [review-dir]
12	#   review-dir  defaults to docs/skill-review (relative to the repo root)
13	#
14	# WHAT COUNTS AS A CHANGED SKILL. The gate reads the push range (the same base ladder as
15	# check-prover-record.sh: LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE if set — CI passes github.event.before, a planted
16	# test passes the base commit — else origin/main, else HEAD~1) and looks at every changed file
17	# under skills/. A skill is SUBSTANTIVELY changed when a changed file under it carries at least one
18	# added or removed content line that is NOT a version stamp.
19	#
20	# THE VERSION-STAMP CARVE-OUT (crucial). scripts/stamp-versions.py rewrites two things in a skill's
21	# SKILL.md at every version bump: the frontmatter `  version: X.Y.Z` line, and the in-text
22	# `live-spec-base (vX.Y.Z)` base-reference. That is a machine-stamped copy of one fact (the pack
23	# version), not a change to the skill's instructions, so it owes NO skill-creator review. A changed
24	# line is EXEMPT when it is exactly the frontmatter version line, or when it carries the
25	# base-reference token — so a file whose ONLY changed lines are stamps is not a substantive change.
26	# A change to the skill's body / instructions / logic leaves a non-stamp changed line, and that is
27	# what requires the review.
28	#
29	# THE RECORD. For each substantively-changed skill <name>, the gate requires a COMMITTED record
30	# under <review-dir> that (1) names the skill, (2) carries the SKILL-REVIEW marker and a Verdict:
31	# line, and (3) is FRESH — THAT RECORD'S OWN commit is at least as new as the skill's own last
32	# change (equal, or an ancestor of the record's commit — the record may ship in the same commit as
33	# the skill change it covers). A stale record from an earlier review does not cover a later
34	# change, mirroring check-prover-record.sh's freshness rule, and a fresh but unrelated commit
35	# elsewhere under <review-dir> does not launder a stale match for THIS skill either — each
36	# candidate record is checked on its own commit, not the directory's.
37	#
38	# Exit 0 = every substantively-changed skill carries a fresh review record (or none changed).
39	# Exit 1 = at least one substantively-changed skill has no matching record.
40	
41	set -euo pipefail
42	
43	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
44	cd "$REPO_ROOT"
45	
46	REVIEW_DIR="${1:-docs/skill-review}"
47	
48	# The frontmatter stamp: `  version: X.Y.Z` on its own. The base-reference stamp: any line carrying
49	# the `live-spec-base` (vX.Y.Z) token. A changed line matching either is a pure stamp.
50	STAMP_VERSION_RE='^  version: [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$'
51	STAMP_BASEREF_RE='`live-spec-base` \(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\)'
52	
53	# --- resolve the push range's base (same ladder as check-prover-record.sh) ---
54	DIFF_BASE=""
55	if [ -n "${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE:-}" ] && \
56	   [ "${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE}" != "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] && \
57	   git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE}^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
58	  DIFF_BASE="${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE}"
59	elif git rev-parse --verify --quiet origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1; then
60	  DIFF_BASE="origin/main"
61	elif git rev-parse --verify --quiet "HEAD~1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
62	  DIFF_BASE="HEAD~1"
63	fi
64	
65	if [ -z "$DIFF_BASE" ]; then
66	  echo "OK (skill review): no push range resolves (single-commit tree, no origin/main) — no skill"
67	  echo "  change can be measured, so none is required."
68	  exit 0
69	fi
70	
71	# --- which skills changed substantively in the range? ---
72	changed_files="$(git diff --name-only "$DIFF_BASE" HEAD -- 'skills/' || true)"
73	
74	substantive_skills=""
75	while IFS= read -r f; do
76	  [ -z "$f" ] && continue
77	  # the changed content lines for this file (added or removed), minus the +++/--- headers
78	  diff_body="$(git diff -U0 "$DIFF_BASE" HEAD -- "$f" | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -Ev '^(\+\+\+|---)' || true)"
79	  # drop the leading +/-, then strip out stamp lines and blank lines; whatever remains is substance
80	  remainder="$(printf '%s\n' "$diff_body" \
81	      | sed -E 's/^[+-]//' \
82	      | grep -Ev "$STAMP_VERSION_RE" \
83	      | grep -Ev "$STAMP_BASEREF_RE" \
84	      | grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*$' || true)"
85	  if [ -n "$remainder" ]; then
86	    # skills/<name>/... -> <name>
87	    name="$(printf '%s' "$f" | sed -E 's#^skills/([^/]+)/.*#\1#')"
88	    case " $substantive_skills " in
89	      *" $name "*) : ;;
90	      *) substantive_skills="$substantive_skills $name" ;;
91	    esac
92	  fi
93	done <<< "$changed_files"
94	
95	substantive_skills="$(printf '%s' "$substantive_skills" | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//')"
96	
97	if [ -z "$substantive_skills" ]; then
98	  echo "OK (skill review): the push changes no skill body (a pure version-stamp diff owes no review),"
99	  echo "  so the skill-creator-review gate stands down by name (SPEC INV-208)."
100	  exit 0
101	fi
102	
103	fail=0
104	for name in $substantive_skills; do
105	  skill_commit="$(git log -1 --format=%H -- "skills/$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
106	
107	  # Find a COMMITTED record that names this skill, carries the marker, carries a verdict, AND is
108	  # itself fresh enough — its own commit is at or after the skill's last change. Checking the whole
109	  # review dir's newest commit here (its earlier shape) let an unrelated same-day record elsewhere
110	  # under docs/skill-review/ wave through a match on a different, stale record for THIS skill: the
111	  # loop below took the first name+marker+verdict hit in `git ls-files` order (oldest-dated file
112	  # first, since filenames sort lexically), and the directory-wide freshness check then compared
113	  # against a commit that record never carried. Two records for 'live-spec-base' — 2026-07-17 and a
114	  # same-day-as-the-skill-change 2026-08-09 one — reproduced exactly this: the gate matched the
115	  # 2026-07-17 record and called it fresh off the directory's unrelated last commit (finding 7,
116	  # docs/prover/2026-08-09-the-culling-first-day.md). Each candidate's OWN commit is checked now, and
117	  # the loop keeps looking past a stale match instead of stopping on the first name hit.
118	  matched=""
119	  while IFS= read -r rec; do
120	    [ -z "$rec" ] && continue
121	    case "$(basename "$rec")" in README.md) continue ;; esac   # the home doc is not a record

2	"""rotate-doc.py — the mechanism that splits and rotates the pack's append-only working documents
3	(SPEC INV-209, ROADMAP rows 390 + 392, the growth/grooming family).
4	
5	ROADMAP.md, JOURNAL.md, PRODUCT_SPEC.md, and TEST_MATRIX.md grow with every landing until a guard's
6	scan and a grep run slow (the owner's word, 2026-07-17 ~18:25). This tool moves a document's fully-closed
7	portion into a dated archive under docs/queue-archive/ and leaves a manifest line in the live file, so
8	the live file keeps only live material and the archive keeps everything — base rule 10's superseded-file-
9	moves-to-attic-with-a-manifest law, applied to a document's own closed portion. Nothing is lost, and a
10	row cited by number across the tree stays findable: the archive keeps each rotated row's `| n |` line and
11	the manifest maps every rotated number to its archive. The gate guardrails/check-doc-rotation.py guards
12	that the move lost nothing.
13	
14	DONE convention (no redundant marker minted, SPEC INV-209): a ROADMAP row is ROTATABLE when its status
15	cell already carries a terminal word — `landed`, `decided`, `declined`, or `superseded` — and carries NO open signal —
16	`queued`, `in-work`, `deferred`, `open`, `field leg`, `field-gated`, `intended`, `[target]` (an unbuilt
17	leg), `waiting`, or `half landed`. A row that shows both (a build leg landed with a field or machine leg
18	still open) is half-done and is never rotated. The tool HALTS rather than
19	rotate a row it cannot read as fully closed, so a wrong `--rows` argument never buries live work.
20	
21	Usage:
22	  rotate-doc.py --doc ROADMAP.md --rows 14,27,33         rotate the named closed rows (batch path).
23	  rotate-doc.py --doc ROADMAP.md --rows 14-20            a row range.
24	  rotate-doc.py --doc ROADMAP.md --close-row 480         the queue's monthly closing-commit move (see below).
25	  rotate-doc.py --doc ROADMAP.md --close-row 480 --month 2026-07   pin the month (default: this month).
26	  rotate-doc.py --base DIR                               resolve paths under DIR (default: repo root).
27	  rotate-doc.py --date 2026-07-18                        stamp the batch archive/manifest (default: today).
28	  rotate-doc.py --doc ROADMAP.md --close-row 480 --dry-run   print what would move, change nothing.
29	
30	Two paths, one mechanism:
31	
32	  - the BATCH path (`--rows`): the original milestone rotation of a fully-closed portion into a
33	    day-named archive `rotated-ROADMAP-YYYY-MM-DD.md`, one manifest line per rotation. It gates each
34	    named row on the old-format closed signal (never buries live work). Used by the legacy archives and
35	    the other growable docs' portions; kept working unchanged.
36	
37	  - the CLOSING-COMMIT path (`--close-row N`): the queue's live-body law (SPEC INV-276, ROADMAP row 480).
38	    When a wish reaches a terminal exit its row moves out of the body in the same commit that closes it,
39	    into the CURRENT MONTH's archive `rotated-ROADMAP-YYYY-MM.md` — created with the standard header when

2	"""check-doc-bound.py — gate z: every growable working doc stays within its declared bound (SPEC
3	INV-234, ROADMAP row 392, the growth-law family).
4	
5	Everything that can grow declares the number that bounds it and the watcher that reads it. INV-41 states
6	the shape — a budget plus the watcher that reds past it — and this lifts it to the four large working
7	documents: PRODUCT_SPEC.md, ROADMAP.md, TEST_MATRIX.md, and JOURNAL.md, which grow with every landing
8	until a guard's scan and a grep run slow (the owner's word, 2026-07-17 ~18:25, at roughly half a
9	megabyte each). Each declares a byte ceiling with a recorded reason in `guardrails/doc-bounds.json`, and
10	this gate reds a doc past its ceiling.
11	
12	It COMPOSES with the doc-rotation gate (gate t, `guardrails/check-doc-rotation.py`, SPEC INV-209):
13	crossing the bound is what earns a rotation, and the rotation is the remedy the red points to. A doc
14	rotated TODAY — carrying a `<!-- rotated-manifest -->` block naming an archive dated today — passes even
15	over its ceiling, since the grooming that shrinks the live file back under the bound has just been
16	applied. A rotation from another day does not clear today's overflow.
17	
18	Three states, one gate:
19	  (a) size <= bound                                    -> pass.
20	  (b) size > bound AND freshly rotated today           -> pass (the remedy applied; compose with gate t).
21	  (c) size > bound, no fresh rotation, no raised bound -> RED, pointing at the two remedies:
22	      rotate the closed rows out (scripts/rotate-doc.py), or raise the ceiling in doc-bounds.json with a
23	      recorded reason.
24	
25	A bound rises only with a recorded reason: every declared entry must carry a non-empty `reason`, and a
26	bound with none reds (the raise discipline, kin of the debt cap's deliberate-visible-edit rule). The
27	ceilings are seeded ABOVE the current file sizes with rotation headroom, so this very gate never reds
28	the already-large tree; the ratchet's direction is down, reset by rotation, never a silent creep up.
29	
30	Usage:
31	  check-doc-bound.py                              push mode: read guardrails/doc-bounds.json at the repo.
32	  check-doc-bound.py --base DIR                   resolve the declared docs under DIR (default: repo root).
33	  check-doc-bound.py --bounds FILE               read the bounds from FILE (fixtures).
34	  check-doc-bound.py --today YYYY-MM-DD           override today's date (fixtures; default: the real day).
35	"""
36	import argparse
37	import datetime
38	import json
39	import os
40	import re
41	import sys
42	
43	MANIFEST_OPEN = "<!-- rotated-manifest -->"
44	MANIFEST_CLOSE = "<!-- /rotated-manifest -->"
45	# an archive path names its rotation date: rotated-<doc>-YYYY-MM-DD.md
46	ARCHIVE_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"rotated-.*?-(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\.md")
47	
48	
49	def repo_root():
50	    import subprocess
51	    try:
52	        out = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
53	                                      stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True).strip()
54	        if out:
55	            return out
56	    except Exception:
57	        pass
58	    return os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
59	
60	
61	def rotated_today(doc_text, today):
62	    """True when the doc carries a rotation manifest naming an archive dated `today` — the fresh-rotation
63	    grace that composes with gate t (SPEC INV-209)."""
64	    for block in re.findall(re.escape(MANIFEST_OPEN) + r"(.*?)" + re.escape(MANIFEST_CLOSE),
65	                            doc_text, re.S):
66	        for m in ARCHIVE_DATE_RE.finditer(block):
67	            if m.group(1) == today:
68	                return True
69	    return False
70	
71	
72	def main(argv=None):
73	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="the growable-doc bound watcher (SPEC INV-234)")
74	    ap.add_argument("--base", default=None)
75	    ap.add_argument("--bounds", default=None)
76	    ap.add_argument("--today", default=None)
77	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
78	
79	    root = args.base or repo_root()
80	    bounds_path = args.bounds or os.path.join(root, "guardrails", "doc-bounds.json")
81	    today = args.today or datetime.date.today().isoformat()
82	
83	    with open(bounds_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
84	        cfg = json.load(f)
85	    docs = cfg.get("docs", {})
86	
87	    if not docs:
88	        print("doc-bound: the bounds file declares no growable doc — a check that looks at nothing is "
89	              "not a pass (SPEC INV-218 kin). Declare the four working docs in %s." % bounds_path)
90	        return 1
91	
92	    violations = []
93	    for name, entry in sorted(docs.items()):
94	        bound = entry.get("max_bytes")
95	        reason = (entry.get("reason") or "").strip()
96	        path = os.path.join(root, name)
97	        if not reason:
98	            violations.append("%s declares a bound with no recorded reason — a bound rises only with a "
99	                              "recorded reason." % name)
100	            continue
101	        if bound is None:
102	            violations.append("%s declares no max_bytes." % name)
103	            continue
104	        if not os.path.isfile(path):
105	            violations.append("%s is declared a growable doc but is absent under %s." % (name, root))
106	            continue
107	        size = os.path.getsize(path)
108	        if size <= bound:
109	            continue
110	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
111	            text = f.read()
112	        if rotated_today(text, today):
113	            continue  # the remedy was applied today — compose with gate t (INV-209).
114	        violations.append(
115	            "%s is %d bytes, past its declared bound of %d, with no rotation dated %s. Remedy: rotate "
116	            "the closed rows out (scripts/rotate-doc.py) so the live file shrinks back under the bound, "
117	            "or raise max_bytes in %s with a recorded reason."
118	            % (name, size, bound, today, os.path.basename(bounds_path)))
119	
120	    if violations:
121	        print("doc-bound (gate z): %d growable doc(s) past bound (SPEC INV-234, ROADMAP 392):"
122	              % len(violations))
123	        for v in violations:
124	            print("  " + v)
125	        return 1
126	
127	    print("doc-bound (gate z): OK — every growable doc sits within its declared bound (or was rotated "
128	          "today); %d docs read." % len(docs))
129	    return 0
130	
131	
132	if __name__ == "__main__":
133	    sys.exit(main())

## Decisions — where they live

The pack's decisions live in three homes already. The first is the queue's dated rows, each landing's
verdicts inline. The second is JOURNAL.md's chapters, which hold the why. The third is DECISIONS.md's
open-decision entries: D-1, D-6, D-7, covering attic layout, pair queue view, and engine-fact
citation. They moved there from the retired Formal index at the 4.0.0 format migration, and the spec's
`[GAP: ...]` lines now point to them. This section is the doc's one entry point to them, and it holds
pointers rather than the decisions themselves. Structure-changing decisions also appear in the
architecture prover record at `docs/prover/architecture-prover-record.md`, one line each. Every full
pass that proves this document beside the spec appends its dated row to that prover record (INV-116).
Those passes run at an M-1 milestone gate and at an M-6 push gate. The gate walk carries the duty, so
the record stays current with the architecture's freshness rule rather than trailing it. The M-1
milestone gate also runs the design review on the re-proven spec (INV-141). Its dated design-review
record lands in `docs/design-review/`, beside the prover record. A structure-changing design decision
it settles appears in that prover record's rows like any other.

*Coverage rule (walked at matrix derivation): every spec anchor appears in some node's "owns" column. An
orphan fact means a missing node or a missing assignment. A node that owns nothing has no spec backing,
and that is itself a finding. Mechanized in `tests/test_traceability.py`.*

**Boundary health — a typical request lands in one node (SPEC INV-128).** A right node boundary shows
one sign. An edit inside a node leaves its neighbours untouched, so a typical request's footprint is
single-module. When requests repeatedly cut across the same several nodes, the boundary sits in the
wrong place. The signal is the entry impact read recording a cross-cutting footprint on the same node
pair again and again. The recorded footprints are the evidence a boundary move rests on. A boundary
moves only through the architecture step and its re-prove, as a restructure row [E-14, and INV-37 in
the spec]. It never moves on a guess, and it never stays wrong in denial while the cross-cuts pile up.
The **cross-cut counter** mechanizes the signal. `guardrails/crosscut_counter.py` reads the closed
queue's cross-cutting landings. It counts, per unordered node pair, how many cross-cutting changes
touched both nodes. A pair reaching the threshold, 3 by default and tunable, is flagged for the MINOR
audit as a boundary-move candidate. That is the mechanized form of "seen twice, own it" (base rule 19)
applied to boundaries. The flag is an audit signal, never a per-push red. The count is evidence the
MINOR audit weighs. The boundary still moves only through the architecture step and its re-prove
[INV-37]. This law states the bar and the signal; the counter is the recorded footprints made
countable.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check-no-history.py — the no-history / provenance gate (SPEC INV-253).

UNARMED until the spec-format conversion delivery (INV-270); no default file, the document is named on
the command line.

THE LAW (FORMAT.md law 6, INV-253): the spec states today's behaviour only. Dates, provenance, and the
reasons behind past choices live in `JOURNAL.md`, not in the spec. A dated note or a provenance
sentence in the spec BODY is a defect and moves to the journal.

This gate reds the body (the requirements, from the first requirement on — the preamble and glossary
are exempt, as the preamble may state what the codes are and the glossary may define `journal` in
terms of the history it holds) on:

  - a DATE: an ISO date (2026-07-22), a month-name-and-number (July 2026), or a bare four-digit year.
  - a RECORDED-WORD phrase: "his word", "he said", "on his OK", "her word", and their kin — a decision
    attributed to a person's recorded say, which belongs in the journal.
  - a HISTORY phrase: "back in <year>", "as of <year>", "used to be", "formerly", "previously renamed",
    "flipped on", "(v… , <year>)" — a sentence narrating a past state rather than today's.

Deliberately NOT flagged: "supersede(d)", which the attic requirement uses for today's behaviour, and
"history" / "past choices", which the glossary may name when defining the journal. The precise reason
behind a requirement is a cold-reader / journal concern; this gate catches the mechanical date and
attribution markers.

Usage:
  check-no-history.py <document.md> [<part.md> ...]
Exit 0 when the body carries no date or provenance marker (printing the reach line, INV-269); exit 1
naming each. Stdlib only.
"""
import os
import re
import sys

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, SCRIPT_DIR)
import specformat as sf  # noqa: E402
from nonempty_input import require_nonempty, VacuousInputError  # noqa: E402

CHECK = "check-no-history"

MONTHS = ("January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December")
PATTERNS = [
    ("date", re.compile(r"\b(?:19|20)\d\d-\d\d-\d\d\b")),
    ("date", re.compile(r"\b(?:%s)\s+\d" % MONTHS)),
    ("date", re.compile(r"\b\d{1,2}\s+(?:%s)\b" % MONTHS)),
    ("year", re.compile(r"\b(?:19|20)\d\d\b")),
    ("recorded-word", re.compile(r"\b(?:his|her|their)\s+word\b", re.I)),
    ("recorded-word", re.compile(r"\bhe\s+said\b|\bshe\s+said\b", re.I)),
    ("recorded-word", re.compile(r"\bon\s+(?:his|her|their)\s+ok\b", re.I)),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check-every-gate-can-fail.py — every push gate carries a known-red proof (SPEC INV-212, gate w).

THE LAW behind it: a gate that cannot red is a check that looks at nothing — it reports green
because it never fires. This movement paid for the lesson: the authority-anchor gate shipped hollow
(commit 8a0209f rebuilt it), reporting green without reaching the surfaces it claimed to inspect,
and a worker's false "zero violations" was the same disease, a claim that protected nothing because
nothing could make it fail. So every gate the push chain runs must carry a KNOWN-RED PROOF: a
committed red-first test that drives that gate's own check to a non-zero exit, so the gate is shown
to fire. A gate with no such proof is itself the finding.

This check enumerates the gate letters guardrails/pre-push invokes — its "-- gate X:" markers, the
same enumeration check-ci-mirror.sh (gate u) reads — and requires each classified in
guardrails/gate-red-proofs.json as one of:

  * a "proof" — a red-first test `<file>::<function>` that drives the gate's check to red, tied to
    that gate by a `reds` token (usually the check's basename) the proof file must reference; or
  * "covered" — a gate that invokes no independent check of its own but rides another gate's red
    (gate c rides the pytest suite, gate b), declared with the reason it carries no separate fixture.

A registered proof is verified by reading its structure, since the suite already runs it under gate b
(exactly as check-ci-mirror.sh's own red-proof runs there): the proof file exists, the named function
is defined in it, the `reds` token appears in the file (tying the proof to this gate's check), and the
function body carries a non-zero-exit assertion, so a bare "the gate ships" presence test cannot pass
as a red proof.

A gate marker classified in none of the three maps reds — the self-widening teeth, so a gate added
later without a proof cannot slip through. A "covered" entry with no reason reds — papering over a
hollow gate is the one thing this gate exists to stop. And a gate that genuinely can never be made to
red by construction is a finding, not a carve-out: the "cannot_red" map exists so such a gate is named
loudly and reds this check, never silently waved through. A registry key naming a letter that is no
local gate is itself drift and reds, like a stale CI carve-out (INV-210).

This is the guard over the guards — a structural scan kin of config-health (INV-175) and the CI-mirror
gate (INV-210).
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(SCRIPT_DIR)

PREPUSH = os.environ.get("GATE_PROOFS_PREPUSH", os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "guardrails", "pre-push"))
REGISTRY = os.environ.get("GATE_PROOFS_JSON", os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "guardrails", "gate-red-proofs.json"))

GATE_MARKER = re.compile(r"-- gate ([a-z]{1,2}):")   # the chain outgrew one letter per gate

# A genuine non-zero-exit assertion, in the idioms the suite's red-proof tests use. It matches an
# assertion that the check FAILED (returncode 1/2, or not 0), or a call to a red-asserting helper.
# It deliberately does NOT match a green assertion (returncode 0) or a mere function name, so a bare
# presence test cannot pass as a red proof.
RED_ASSERT = re.compile(
    r"assert_red\(|expect_red\("
    r"|assertNotEqual\([^)\n]*(?:returncode|\bcode)\b[^)\n]*,\s*0\b"
    r"|assertEqual\([^)\n]*(?:returncode|\bcode)\b[^)\n]*,\s*[12]\b"
    r"|(?:returncode|\bcode)\s*!=\s*0\b"
    r"|(?:returncode|\bcode)\s*==\s*[12]\b"
)

261	## Requirement 245: Everything growable declares the number that bounds it
262	
263	**Context:** When a thing just grows without end — a script, a spec, a test matrix — the system cannot do nothing. Where a node's fitness asks whether a file holds one thing or several, this asks whether a thing has grown past what it may weigh, where size is the signal and needs its own declared number. Each of the four large working documents declares a byte ceiling with a recorded reason, and a watcher reds a document past its ceiling.
264	
265	**User Story:** As a person watching a document grow without bound, I want each growable artifact to declare a byte ceiling with a reason and a watcher to read it, so that crossing the bound earns a rotation while a silent creep upward has no door.

## Requirement 245: Everything growable declares the number that bounds it

**Context:** When a thing just grows without end — a script, a spec, a test matrix — the system cannot do nothing. Where a node's fitness asks whether a file holds one thing or several, this asks whether a thing has grown past what it may weigh, where size is the signal and needs its own declared number. Each of the four large working documents declares a byte ceiling with a recorded reason, and a watcher reds a document past its ceiling.

**User Story:** As a person watching a document grow without bound, I want each growable artifact to declare a byte ceiling with a reason and a watcher to read it, so that crossing the bound earns a rotation while a silent creep upward has no door.

### Acceptance Criteria

**Case: a ceiling with a recorded reason**

1. The system *shall* have each of the four named working documents — the spec (PRODUCT_SPEC.md), the queue (ROADMAP.md), the test matrix (TEST_MATRIX.md), and the journal (JOURNAL.md) — declare a byte ceiling with a non-empty recorded reason in `guardrails/doc-bounds.json`, and *shall* red a document past its ceiling. [INV-234, INV-41]
2. *if* a declared bound carries no reason, *then* the system *shall* red it. [INV-234]

**Case: rotation is the remedy**

3. *when* a document over its ceiling carries a manifest naming an archive dated the same day, the system *shall* pass it, since the grooming that shrinks it back under the bound has just been applied. [INV-234, INV-209]
4. The system *shall* seed the ceilings above the current file sizes with rotation headroom, and *shall* let a ceiling rise only with a recorded reason. [INV-234]

**Case: the queue archives at each closing commit**

5. The system *shall*, for the queue (ROADMAP.md), take the closing commit as its archiving cadence, hold its byte ceiling as a backstop, and grow its manifest one line per monthly archive file; the spec, the test matrix, and the journal keep their byte-ceiling rotation unchanged. [INV-234, INV-276]

# MIGRATION — the catch-up walk

This is the operating guide for the catch-up walk: the procedure an already-adopted host's own session runs to bring the host's documents and records onto the current package version. A package release that owes its hosts actions lands one dated chapter at the end of this file; the walk reads the chapter chain and applies it under the owner's gate, preserving every recorded fact. Nothing outside a host's own session ever writes that host's repo (INV-10).

The bracketed codes on this page — `INV-10`, `A-11`, `E-32` and the rest — name rules in `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`. `PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md` gives each code's location in that document. A feature code such as `F-catchup` carries no index row and sits on its requirement's heading.

The walk is the executable projection of Requirement 180 in `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, "The catch-up sequence brings an adopted host onto the current pack". Its codes are F-catchup, A-11, and INV-89 through INV-92. The spec states the facts; this guide states the moves.

## When to run this

The ask arrives in any wording. It might read "re-layout the documentation" or "catch up to the current pack"; it names no procedure, so the package names one, and that procedure is this walk.

Route the ask before doing anything else. A host that never adopted the pack goes to adoption (`adopt/ADOPT.md`) for the first-adoption phases. A host that already adopted goes to this catch-up walk. A single-document edit belongs to the ordinary docs-only door, which `skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md` states. A restructure of the host's own product is the host's own queue row through the build pipeline. This walk fires only to move an adopted host's own live-spec documents and records onto a newer package version. The catch-up walk fires only when the host's recorded package version is behind the current package VERSION. A docs restructure that carries no version delta is the host's own queue row through its pipeline, whatever wording the ask used. The trigger wordings are examples under this test. A wording never decides the routing; the version delta decides. (INV-110)

## The walk

The walk runs four phases in order (A-11). Its plan and its working artifacts live in the host's `.live-spec/adopt/` through the whole walk, tracked in git as the run's audit trail.

## Phase 1 — orient on the delta

1. Read the host's installed-set record, which sits in the host's `.live-spec/` directory (SPEC M-7), and the tree as found.
2. Read the package's current `VERSION` and journal, and the migration chapters below.
3. Build the work list: the ordered chain of migration chapters from the host's recorded package version to the current one (see "Migration chapters"), plus any drift the tree shows against what those chapters expect. A record that carries no readable package version — commit pins, or no record at all — starts the chain at the earliest chapter; every step's already-done check makes over-application harmless (INV-89).
4. Treat every precondition written in this guide as a claim to check against the tree. Where a written precondition and the tree disagree, the tree is the truth.
5. Name the founding questions this host has never answered: read the host profile at `.live-spec/profile.md` for its `founding.set-version`, against the current set in `scripts/founding-questions.json`, and list each question added after the host's recorded version — the agent card at `.live-spec/agent.md` (SPEC E-32) among them for a host that founded before it. A host with no `founding.set-version` line founded before the set was versioned and owes every question. Each gap rides the plan for the owner to answer, and the walk records the current set version once answered; a never-answered question is surfaced for the owner, answered on no one's behalf (SPEC INV-227, the duty binds forward INV-159).

## Phase 2 — plan, behind the owner's gate

Write one plan document into the host's `.live-spec/adopt/`, where it lives through the whole walk. It lists every file that moves, merges, or retires, every record that reformats, every rename offered, and every open conflict. It names the baseline commit of Phase 3 as the walk's restore point and states the one restore command that returns the host to the pre-walk state.
